html:
The Lines of Torres Vedras were a chain of forts and earthworks built in secret north of Lisbon in 1809 and 1810 by Portuguese labourers under British command, to protect the capital from Napoleon's armies.

France had invaded Portugal in 1807, and the royal family fled to Brazil. In 1810 Marshal Masséna led a third French invasion. The Duke of Wellington pulled his British and Portuguese army back behind the lines, while the countryside in front was stripped of food.

Masséna found the lines too strong to attack. His army starved through the winter and retreated in March 1811, losing many thousands. It was a turning point of the Peninsular War in Iberia. Wellington went on to drive the French out of Spain. It was a moment of the old alliance.
sum: The Lines of Torres Vedras were a chain of forts and earthworks built in secret north of Lisbon in 1809 and 1810 by Portuguese labourers under British command, to protect the capital from Napoleon's armies.
